reads.note: Read via creatorGates(currentSession) from src/lib/api/mocks/session.ts, not through subscriptionApi — a second, session-scoped source for tier/slots that overlaps with Subscription.plan.tier. Component resolves the display tier as `subscription?.plan.tier ?? gates.tier ?? 'basic'`, i.e. Subscription is authoritative when present and CreatorSession is only a fallback.

src/types/subscription.ts PLANS constant — a hardcoded 2-entry (basic/pro) client-side catalog, not fetched from any API at all (no SEAM comment, no mocks/ file). Every price/split/feature-list value the screen shows is sourced from this static object, not from a backend read. Flagged because docs/05_CONVENTIONS.md requires canonical prices to be looked up server-side, never client-supplied — this screen currently has zero backend dependency for pricing.

SEAM-tagged (SubscriptionManagement.tsx:23-30) but not promoted to mocks/subscription.ts — stands in for GET /api/hub/creator-subscription/history, which does not exist anywhere in the mock data layer. Rendered only on the desktop layout (BillingHistoryCard, shown whenever state !== 'none').

actions.name: upgradeToPro
actions.note: Called with no arguments by both payAndGoPro() (upgrade screen CTA) and startTier('pro') (resubscribe screen). SEAM comment on the mock says 'POST /api/hub/creator-subscription (tier=pro)' — the tier is implied by which client method is called, never passed as an explicit payload field client-side.

actions.name: downgradeToBasic
actions.note: Called with no arguments by handleDowngrade() (cancel sheet's 'Move to Basic' quick action, pro tier only) and startTier('basic') (resubscribe screen). SEAM: 'POST /api/hub/creator-subscription (tier=basic)'. Doc says this both starts a fresh Basic term after expiry (no proration) AND downgrades an active Pro subscription mid-term — two materially different real-world transactions currently collapsed onto the same mock call with no distinguishing payload.

actions.name: retryPayment
actions.note: SEAM: POST /api/hub/creator-subscription/retry. Retries payment on the CURRENT tier after a past-due failure. Mock always succeeds and resets state to 'active' — no failure/still-declined response path exists.

actions.name: cancelPro
actions.note: SEAM: DELETE /api/hub/creator-subscription. Despite the name, this is 'stop renewing' for either tier (called from the cancel sheet's 'Stop renewing' button regardless of current tier) — it sets cancelsAt to +365 days and leaves state as 'active' until that date, it does not immediately terminate the subscription.

actions.name: updateCard
actions.note: SEAM: POST /api/hub/creator-subscription/card. Mock only ever returns the same last4 it was sent — no real payment-method tokenization/verification modeled. Card sheet itself offers a hardcoded choice between two literal last4 values ('4412','9021'), not a real card-entry form.

no — same reason as past_due: no code path in the mock layer ever sets state to 'expired', despite the UI (design frame 5) being fully built for it, including the 'Start a tier again' CTA that would lead to the resubscribe screen
no — same reason again; also structurally unlikely since the mock session (src/lib/api/mocks/session.ts) always seeds an existing subscribed pro creator, not a plan-less one

uiStatesDesigned: 1 · Current — tier, renewal, slots, limits (design/screens/WAWU Subscription Management.dc.html, frame 1: active/basic billing view)
2 · Upgrade — the split shown against real sales (frame 2: Move to Pro screen with proration math)
3 · Upgrade paid — proration and next renewal stated (frame 3: post-payment confirmation sheet)
4 · Past due — two lists, no ambiguity (frame 4: declined-card banner + still-working/paused lists)
5 · Expired — work, money, perks, answered separately (frame 5: expired billing view)
6 · Cancel — consequences, then a cheaper option (frame 6: 'Stop renewing?' sheet with downgrade offer)

D9 · Subscription — current plan and the upgrade case, side by side (design/screens/desktop/WAWU Desktop Shell.dc.html: desktop layout reusing the left column for past-due/expired/cancel; includes a Billing History card and a 'Pause for a month' button that has no corresponding SubscriptionState or subscriptionApi method — the component's own code comment documents substituting downgrade-to-basic for it since no pause state exists)
